question: Which boiler is serviced first, Wren or Tern?
system: You will answer a question about a fictional scenario. Use only the information supplied in the scenario. Answer briefly.

messages.content:
Document 1
The plant monitoring system is the source of record for equipment readings. Handwritten shift notes are unverified.

Document 2
Boilers are serviced in order of pressure reading, highest first.
Plant monitoring system: Boiler Wren pressure reading: 72 psi.

Document 3
Source: Facilities handbook
Office plants do best with steady routines rather than bursts of attention. Most common desk plants prefer bright, indirect light, so a spot near a window but out of the harshest afternoon sun usually works well. Before watering, press a finger into the soil; if the top layer still feels damp, wait another day or two. Overwatering is the most frequent cause of yellowing leaves, and it is far easier to revive a thirsty plant than a waterlogged one. Pots should have drainage holes, and saucers should be emptied after watering so roots do not sit in standing water. Dust settles on broad leaves over time and blocks light, so wiping them gently with a soft, damp cloth helps the plant breathe. If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even. Brown, crispy leaf edges often point to dry air from heating or cooling vents, and moving the plant a little farther from the vent can help. When going away for a long weekend, group plants together in a shaded corner so they share humidity and dry out more slowly. Anyone unsure about a particular plant can ask the facilities staff, who are always happy to share care tips.

Document 4
Source: Workplace wellness guide
A comfortable workstation reduces strain and helps people stay focused through the day. Start with the chair: feet should rest flat on the floor or on a footrest, with knees roughly level with the hips. The backrest should support the natural curve of the lower back, and a small cushion can fill the gap if the chair does not. Next, position the screen so the top edge sits at or slightly below eye level, about an arm's length away. Looking slightly downward at the screen is more relaxed for the neck than looking up. The keyboard and mouse should sit close enough that elbows stay near the body and bend at a comfortable angle, with wrists straight rather than bent upward. Laptop users benefit from a separate keyboard and a stand that raises the screen. Lighting matters as well; glare from windows or overhead lights can cause eye fatigue, so tilting the screen or adjusting blinds often helps. Even a well arranged desk cannot replace movement. Standing up, stretching the shoulders, and looking at something far away for a short while gives muscles and eyes a needed break. Small habits like these add up and make long working sessions noticeably more comfortable.

Document 5
Source: Plant monitoring system, May 12
Boiler Tern pressure reading: 84 psi.

Document 6
Source: Break room guidelines
The shared kitchen works best when everyone treats it like a space they would want to walk into themselves. Dishes, mugs, and utensils should be washed, dried, and put away rather than left in the sink for someone else. If the dishwasher is full and clean, unloading it is a small favor that keeps things moving for the next person. Food stored in the refrigerator should be labeled with the owner's name, and anything that is no longer wanted should be taken home or thrown away before it spoils. Strong smelling foods are best reheated briefly and covered, out of consideration for colleagues working nearby. Spills on counters, tables, or the floor should be wiped up right away, and paper towels and cleaning spray are kept under the sink for that purpose. The coffee machine needs a little care too: empty the used grounds, rinse the carafe, and let someone know if supplies are running low. When hosting a celebration with shared treats, leaving a short message about common allergens is a thoughtful touch. Finally, please keep the microwave clean by covering dishes while heating them. A tidy kitchen makes breaks more pleasant for everyone and saves the cleaning crew from avoidable work.

Document 7
Source: Sustainability guide
Sorting waste correctly keeps recycling streams clean and makes it far more likely that materials are actually reused. Paper and cardboard belong in the blue bins, but only when they are dry and free of food. Flatten boxes before placing them in the bin so they take up less room. Greasy pizza boxes, used napkins, and paper towels go with general waste or compost instead, since oil and food residue contaminate paper recycling. Plastic bottles and containers should be emptied and given a quick rinse; caps can usually stay on. Soft plastics such as wrappers and film are not accepted in the standard bins and should go in general waste unless a special collection point is available. Glass jars and bottles go in their own container, and broken glass should be wrapped carefully before disposal so nobody gets hurt. Food scraps, coffee grounds, and tea leaves belong in the compost caddy, which is emptied regularly. Batteries, ink cartridges, and old electronics must never go in ordinary bins; ask the facilities team where the dedicated drop off box is located. When in doubt about an item, it is better to put it in general waste than to risk contaminating a whole load of otherwise clean recycling.

Document 8
Source: Shift notes, May 13
Boiler Tern was reading 61 psi on my rounds.

Question: Which boiler is serviced first, Wren or Tern?

response: Tern is serviced first. Its verified plant monitoring reading is 84 psi, higher than Wren’s 72 psi; the shift note reporting 61 psi is unverified.

Most common desk plants prefer bright, indirect light, so a spot near a window but out of the harshest afternoon sun usually works well. Before watering, press a finger into the soil; if the top layer still feels damp, wait another day or two. Overwatering is the most frequent cause of yellowing leaves, and it is far easier to revive a thirsty plant than a waterlogged one. Pots should have drainage holes, and saucers should be emptied after watering so roots do not sit in standing water. Dust settles on broad leaves over time and blocks light, so wiping them gently with a soft, damp cloth helps the plant breathe. If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even. Brown, crispy leaf edges often point to dry air from heating or cooling vents, and moving the plant a little farther from the vent can help. When going away for a long weekend, group plants together in a shaded corner so they share humidity and dry out more slowly. Anyone unsure about a particular plant can ask the facilities staff, who are always happy to share care tips.

Document 4
Source: Workplace wellness guide
A comfortable workstation reduces strain and helps people stay focused through the day. Start with the chair: feet should rest flat on the floor or on a footrest, with knees roughly level with the hips. The backrest should support the natural curve of the lower back, and a small cushion can fill the gap if the chair does not. Next, position the screen so the top edge sits at or slightly below eye level, about an arm's length away. Looking slightly downward at the screen is more relaxed for the neck than looking up. The keyboard and mouse should sit close enough that elbows stay near the body and bend at a comfortable angle, with wrists straight rather than bent upward. Laptop users benefit from a separate keyboard and a stand that raises the screen. Lighting matters as well; glare from windows or overhead lights can cause eye fatigue, so tilting the screen or adjusting blinds often helps. Even a well arranged desk cannot replace movement. Standing up, stretching the shoulders, and looking at something far away for a short while gives muscles and eyes a needed break. Small habits like these add up and make long working sessions noticeably more comfortable.

Document 5
Source: Booking system, January 6
Atlas budget review date: January 21.

Document 6
Source: Break room guidelines
The shared kitchen works best when everyone treats it like a space they would want to walk into themselves. Dishes, mugs, and utensils should be washed, dried, and put away rather than left in the sink for someone else. If the dishwasher is full and clean, unloading it is a small favor that keeps things moving for the next person. Food stored in the refrigerator should be labeled with the owner's name, and anything that is no longer wanted should be taken home or thrown away before it spoils. Strong smelling foods are best reheated briefly and covered, out of consideration for colleagues working nearby. Spills on counters, tables, or the floor should be wiped up right away, and paper towels and cleaning spray are kept under the sink for that purpose. The coffee machine needs a little care too: empty the used grounds, rinse the carafe, and let someone know if supplies are running low. When hosting a celebration with shared treats, leaving a short message about common allergens is a thoughtful touch. Finally, please keep the microwave clean by covering dishes while heating them. A tidy kitchen makes breaks more pleasant for everyone and saves the cleaning crew from avoidable work.

Document 7
Source: Sustainability guide

The Atlas budget review is rescheduled to January 21.

Document 2
Boilers are serviced in order of pressure reading, highest first.
Plant monitoring system: Boiler Wren pressure reading: 72 psi.

Document 3
Source: Facilities handbook
Office plants do best with steady routines rather than bursts of attention. Most common desk plants prefer bright, indirect light, so a spot near a window but out of the harshest afternoon sun usually works well. Before watering, press a finger into the soil; if the top layer still feels damp, wait another day or two. Overwatering is the most frequent cause of yellowing leaves, and it is far easier to revive a thirsty plant than a waterlogged one. Pots should have drainage holes, and saucers should be emptied after watering so roots do not sit in standing water. Dust settles on broad leaves over time and blocks light, so wiping them gently with a soft, damp cloth helps the plant breathe. If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even. Brown, crispy leaf edges often point to dry air from heating or cooling vents, and moving the plant a little farther from the vent can help. When going away for a long weekend, group plants together in a shaded corner so they share humidity and dry out more slowly. Anyone unsure about a particular plant can ask the facilities staff, who are always happy to share care tips.

Document 4
Source: Workplace wellness guide
A comfortable workstation reduces strain and helps people stay focused through the day. Start with the chair: feet should rest flat on the floor or on a footrest, with knees roughly level with the hips. The backrest should support the natural curve of the lower back, and a small cushion can fill the gap if the chair does not. Next, position the screen so the top edge sits at or slightly below eye level, about an arm's length away. Looking slightly downward at the screen is more relaxed for the neck than looking up. The keyboard and mouse should sit close enough that elbows stay near the body and bend at a comfortable angle, with wrists straight rather than bent upward. Laptop users benefit from a separate keyboard and a stand that raises the screen. Lighting matters as well; glare from windows or overhead lights can cause eye fatigue, so tilting the screen or adjusting blinds often helps. Even a well arranged desk cannot replace movement. Standing up, stretching the shoulders, and looking at something far away for a short while gives muscles and eyes a needed break. Small habits like these add up and make long working sessions noticeably more comfortable.

Document 5
Source: Plant monitoring system, May 12
Boiler Tern pressure reading: 84 psi.

Document 6
Source: Break room guidelines
The shared kitchen works best when everyone treats it like a space they would want to walk into themselves. Dishes, mugs, and utensils should be washed, dried, and put away rather than left in the sink for someone else. If the dishwasher is full and clean, unloading it is a small favor that keeps things moving for the next person. Food stored in the refrigerator should be labeled with the owner's name, and anything that is no longer wanted should be taken home or thrown away before it spoils. Strong smelling foods are best reheated briefly and covered, out of consideration for colleagues working nearby. Spills on counters, tables, or the floor should be wiped up right away, and paper towels and cleaning spray are kept under the sink for that purpose. The coffee machine needs a little care too: empty the used grounds, rinse the carafe, and let someone know if supplies are running low. When hosting a celebration with shared treats, leaving a short message about common allergens is a thoughtful touch. Finally, please keep the microwave clean by covering dishes while heating them. A tidy kitchen makes breaks more pleasant for everyone and saves the cleaning crew from avoidable work.

Document 7
Source: Sustainability guide
Sorting waste correctly keeps recycling streams clean and makes it far more likely that materials are actually reused. Paper and cardboard belong in the blue bins, but only when they are dry and free of food. Flatten boxes before placing them in the bin so they take up less room. Greasy pizza boxes, used napkins, and paper towels go with general waste or compost instead, since oil and food residue contaminate paper recycling. Plastic bottles and containers should be emptied and given a quick rinse; caps can usually stay on. Soft plastics such as wrappers and film are not accepted in the standard bins and should go in general waste unless a special collection point is available. Glass jars and bottles go in their own container, and broken glass should be wrapped carefully before disposal so nobody gets hurt. Food scraps, coffee grounds, and tea leaves belong in the compost caddy, which is emptied regularly. Batteries, ink cartridges, and old electronics must never go in ordinary bins; ask the facilities team where the dedicated drop off box is located. When in doubt about an item, it is better to put it in general waste than to risk contaminating a whole load of otherwise clean recycling.

Document 8
Source: Shift notes, May 13
Boiler Tern was reading 84 psi on my rounds.

If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even. Brown, crispy leaf edges often point to dry air from heating or cooling vents, and moving the plant a little farther from the vent can help. The keyboard and mouse should sit close enough that elbows stay near the body and bend at a comfortable angle, with wrists straight rather than bent upward. Laptop users benefit from a separate keyboard and a stand that raises the screen.
